properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued October 16 at 5:09AM EDT until October 16 at 6:00AM EDT by NWS Cleveland OH
properties.description:
SMWCLE

The National Weather Service in Cleveland has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Nearshore and Open waters from Reno Beach OH to Vermilion OH...

* Until 600 AM EDT.

* At 509 AM EDT, downpours producing strong wind gusts were located
along a line extending from near Put-In-Bay to 8 nm northwest of
Sandusky Bay, moving east at 45 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Put-In-Bay, Huron, Kelleys Island, Sandusky Bay, and Western
Vermilion.

* WHEN...From this evening to Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, (1.8 meters), Minor lowland flooding extends
into low areas of the flood plain with no significant impact.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 AM CDT Friday the stage was 2.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
evening to a crest of 6.2 feet late this evening. It will then

- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued early this morning at 445 AM CDT.

properties.description:
An atmospheric river storm system moving into the panhandle is
expected to bring heavy rainfall Thursday night into Friday morning.
This longer duration of heavy rainfall with will allow for river and
creek rises, with minor flooding of small streams expected going into
Friday morning.

* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
continues.

* WHERE...Areas around Montana Creek And Jordan Creek.

* WHEN...Until 130 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas, as
well as area streams and rivers. Water over roadways. Possible
isolated landslides in areas of steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 830 PM AKDT, satellite estimates indicate heavy rain across
the advisory area. Rapid river rises will cause minor flooding of
small streams, especially near Montana Creek And Jordan Creek.
Between 0.75 and 1.25 inches of rain has fallen. The expected
rainfall rate is 0.15-0.3 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall
amounts of 1.5 to 2.5 inches are possible.

- Montana Creek is anticipated to begin to fall below Minor flood
stage by late Friday morning to midday, while Jordan Creek will
stay above Minor flood stage a bit longer into the day, falling
below Minor flood stage by Friday night.

- For Jordan Creek near Juneau:
At 12:00pm the stage was 7.8 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.7 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 9.9 feet is expected around 1:00pm
Friday. Water levels will go above Minor flood stage around
8:00am. Water levels will go below Minor flood stage around
10:00pm.

Impacts:
At 9.2 feet: This is the stage when Jordan Creek is at bankfull and
water will begin to inundate areas along the edges of the creek near
Race Reality and Jordan Square.
At 9.7 feet: Water will inundate the Jordan Square's front and back
parking lots, around Jordan Creek office condominiums with up to one
foot of water. Some residential driveways will be flooded and cut
off.

- For Montana Creek at Back Loop Bridge:
At 12:00pm the stage was 11.2 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 14.7 feet is expected around 7:00am
Friday. Water levels will go above Minor flood stage around
5:00am. Water levels will go below Minor flood stage around
9:00am.

Impacts:
At 14.5 feet: Water begins flowing over the low water crossing on
Montana Creek Road. Bankfull conditions at the gauge with water
starting to inundate adjacent undeveloped fields along Mendenhall
Loop Road.
At 15.5 feet: Up to one half foot of water will flow over the low
water crossing on Montana Creek Road after the community gardens.
Water will approach and begin to inundate yards of residences along
the Northwest side of Mendenhall Loop Road.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

If you live near or along Montana Creek or Jordan Creek stay alert
and be prepared to take action.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 15 at 8:16PM AKDT until October 16 at 6:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Heavy rain has fallen in and around Ketchikan through this afternoon
and will continue into tonight. An additional 1 to 2.5 inches is
expected by daybreak Friday. Reports of flooding and minor slides
have been observed. Ketchikan Creek is at bankfull and could climb
into minor flood stage tonight.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...In and around Ketchikan.

* WHEN...Until 600 AM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas, as
well as area streams and rivers. Water over roadways. Possible
isolated landslides in areas of steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 808 PM AKDT, emergency management reported heavy rain in and
around Ketchikan. Many area streams and rivers are near or at
bankfull and could climb into minor flooding tonight. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Between 2.5 and
4 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to
2.5 inches are possible by daybreak Friday.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Ketchikan, Saxman and Ward Cove.

- For Carlanna Lake Dam in Ketchikan:
At 5:00pm the stage was 522.2 feet.
Flood Stage is 524.0 feet.


For Fawn Lake in Ketchikan:
At 5:00pm the stage was 326.0 feet.


For Ketchikan Lake:
At 5:00pm the stage was 337.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 349.0 feet.

Impacts:
At 348.0 feet: There will be 1 foot of water going over the emergency
spillway at the dam with bankful conditions along Ketchikan Creek.
At 349.0 feet: There will be 2 feet of water going over the emergency
spillway. Minor flooding will occur along Ketchikan Creek mainly
below the Park Ave bridge. There are some tidal effects along Creek
St and flooding could be worse at high tides.

For Ketchikan Powerhouse:
At 5:00pm the stage was 62.2 feet.
Flood Stage is 63.5 feet.

Impacts:
At 63.5 feet: Minor flooding will occur along Ketchikan Creek mainly
below the Park Ave bridge. There are some tidal effects along Creek
St and flooding could be worse at high tides.


For Lake Connell Dam:
At 1:00pm the stage was 250.0 feet.
Flood Stage is 252.0 feet.

Impacts:
At 251.0 feet: Water will begin to approach low lying areas of trails
and picnic areas around Ward Lake.

For Leask Creek at Shelter Cove:
At 5:30pm the stage was 22.2 feet.


For Whitman Lake Dam near Ketchikan:
At 5:00pm the stage was 373.6 feet.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

The ongoing rains could swamp boats. Mariners should check their
vessels immediately.

All residents on or near mountain slopes should be prepared for
possible isolated landslides.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 15 at 9:36PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to remain in Minor Flood
Stage through Friday, as previous heavy rainfall continues to drain
through the basin. However, strong northeasterly winds are forecast
this weekend and will return the river to Moderate Flood Stage, with
a steady increase through Moderate Flood Stage forecast through early
next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Thursday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Thursday was 2.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.3 feet early
Tuesday afternoon. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon EDT.
